text:
Mia: quick sanity check — can someone run a 24h prefix-age distribution sample and share eviction vs age buckets? seeing subtle hit-rate drift and want to rule out an aging-skew artifact. only need a small sample (5%).

Aditya: on it. do you want per-shard breakdown or a cluster aggregate?

Mia: per-shard would be ideal, but cluster aggregate + node anomalies is fine if that's faster. include: sampled_prefixes, age_histogram (bucketed by hours), eviction_rate_by_bucket, fragmentation_score_by_bucket if possible.

Aditya: will run on staging shadow first then prod-shadow. kicking off command: 
```
./tools/kv-sim --sample-rate=0.05 --window=24h --buckets=6 --output=json --nodes=all
```

Aditya: staging run finished — quick paste of aggregate: 
```
 sampled_prefixes: 124,512
 age_buckets_hours: [0-1, 1-4, 4-8, 8-24, 24-72, 72+]
 counts: [54,200, 31,600, 18,300, 12,050, 6,300, 1,862]
 eviction_rate_pct: [0.2, 0.6, 1.8, 4.5, 12.3, 28.9]
 avg_fragmentation: [0.02, 0.03, 0.04, 0.07, 0.12, 0.33]
 pearson(eviction, fragmentation): 0.91
```

Aditya: per-shard highlights: node-3 has 2x eviction in 24-72 vs others, node-7 shows a skewed 0-1h bucket (warm hot-rewrites).

Mia: wow 0.91 corr — that's high. can you attach raw JSON to this thread? also which commit/flags for the runtime used?

Aditya: raw JSON uploaded to S3: s3://rw-inference/kv-samples/1945012345-prefix-age.json (read: eng-runtime). runtime: release/2026-03-08 + kv-prefetch-opt flag enabled.

Samir: fwiw node-3 has been on a slightly older kernel (hotfix pending), might explain higher eviction. also we've seen a scheduled compaction job run around 02:00 UTC yesterday — I'll check compaction logs.

Mia: noted. can we run the same sample but with prefetch disabled on one shadow to see if fragmentation rises? hypothesis: prefetch keeps more small prefixes in memory which changes age curve.

Aditya: good idea. scheduling two prod-shadow runs: one baseline (prefetch on), one prefetched-off. ops-bot will create jobs.

ops-bot: job created: kv-sample-1945012345-baseline -> queued on prod-shadow-1, expected ~12m runtime.

ops-bot: job created: kv-sample-1945012345-no-prefetch -> queued on prod-shadow-2, expected ~11m runtime.

Aditya: baseline done, no-prefetch done. quick diff summary: 
```
baseline_eviction_top_bucket(72+): 28.9% -> no-prefetch: 34.7% (+5.8pp)
baseline_fragmentation_72+: 0.33 -> no-prefetch: 0.41 (+0.08)
pearson(eviction, fragmentation): baseline 0.91 -> no-prefetch 0.88
```

Aditya: node-3 still anomalous even with no-prefetch (eviction 38% in 24-72). looks independent.

Mia: ok, seems prefetch reduces tail eviction and fragmentation modestly but doesn't explain node-3. Samir, can you confirm kernel/compaction timeline for node-3 and whether any heavy background IO (backups) overlapped?

Samir: digging: node-3 had an automated snapshot at 01:58 UTC, compaction window 02:03-02:09, and an emergency GC at 02:12 triggered by oom-killer on aux process. filing incident note on node-3.

Mia: thanks. next steps: 1) schedule targeted eviction/trace on node-3 during low traffic to capture full KV trace, 2) instrument meminfo + io stats during sample window, 3) consider short-term soft-limit on compaction concurrent windows.

Aditya: I'll open a PR with the sample harness plus a small dashboard (age buckets + eviction/fragments) and link here.

Samir: I'll correlate compaction and snapshot schedules and propose a mitigation plan.

Mia: perfect. please ping when PR + dashboards are up. thanks all :thumbsup:
